sections.html:
Floyd County is a small county on the Ohio River, directly across from Louisville, Kentucky, and part of the Louisville metro area. New Albany is both the county seat and the largest city. At about 149 square miles it is the second-smallest county in Indiana by area. Population was 80,484 in 2020 and is estimated at 82,153 for 2025.

The river forms the southern boundary, and part of the county sits in the Knobs, a hilly stretch with dry ridgetops and wet ravines. Older homes near downtown New Albany share the county with new construction, which rose in 2024. Where your lot sits, on a ridge, in a ravine or near the water, will shape how buyers see it.

The Ohio River is the county's biggest weather risk. In January 1937 it reached 60.8 feet at New Albany, and most of the town stood under water for nearly three weeks. New Albany then became the first city in the region to build flood walls. A tornado on March 23, 1917 killed at least 46 people on the north side of the city.

Hillside lots in the Knobs deserve a hard look at drainage before you list. A few steps help any seller here:

  • Ask your insurer whether the parcel is in a mapped flood zone.
  • Keep repair records for any basement or foundation water work.
  • Expect buyers to ask about roof age on older New Albany houses.

Three offices share the work, and all three are in New Albany. The treasurer collects, the assessor values, and the auditor handles rates, calculations and deduction forms. Call before you drive over, since the treasurer's in-person payment counter can be reached at either address shown below.

OfficeAddressPhoneHours
Treasurer120 West Spring Street, Suite 201, or 311 Hauss Square, Room 113(812) 948-5477Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm
Assessor311 Hauss Square, Room B3(812) 948-5420Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm
Auditor120 West Spring Street, Suite 200(812) 948-5433Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm

You can pay several ways. Online payments go through floydcountyintax.com. Phone payments cost $0.65 by e-check or 2.25% by card. Mail to PO Box 3697, Evansville, IN 47736 must be postmarked by the due date. There is a 24-hour drop box, and German American Bank takes payments at any Floyd County branch. First Harrison Bank and Stock Yards Bank no longer do. A bill reprint costs $1.

The assessor also handles property transfers and splits, new construction, sales disclosures and the plat room. The auditor links the homestead, over 65 and mortgage deduction forms on the state's site.

sections.h2: How Floyd County values a house
sections.html:
Tyler Technologies prepared the county's 2025 ratio study, which tests how close assessed values come to sale prices. It used sales from January 1 to December 31, 2024, a year that started strong, slowed in the second half and kept prices high. New construction rose.

  • Overall values went up across the county.
  • Residential, commercial and industrial improved values rose from cost table updates, trending changes and added construction.
  • In that reassessment phase, only sections of Lafayette and New Albany townships were reviewed, against a target of 25% of parcels with a 2% tolerance.
  • A neighborhood with too few sales was grouped with a neighbor of similar economics.
  • A land order went to the county board on February 4, 2025 and took effect that day.

Form 11, the notice of assessment, is mailed by April 30 each year. If the notice shows an error, such as a garage that was torn down or the wrong square footage, you can correct it on page 1 and section III of page 2 of Form 130, the same form used for appeals.

Indiana limits tax to 1% of gross assessed value on a homestead and 2% on other residential property and farmland. Nonresidential and personal property are capped at 3%. The 1% cap depends on having the homestead standard deduction, and a homestead means the house, a garage and up to one acre.

To appeal, file Form 130 with the Floyd County assessor by June 15. The assessor meets with you informally, and the appeals board, which has three members, must hold a hearing within 180 days with at least 30 days of written notice. A written continuance request is due 10 days before the hearing. If the board rules against you or sits past 180 days, take the case to the Indiana Board of Tax Review on Form 131.

While a case is pending you may pay on last year's assessment. Paying less than that makes the installment delinquent, and penalties apply.

A little groundwork keeps a Floyd County sale on schedule.

  1. Call the treasurer at (812) 948-5477 and ask for a payoff balance on every installment, including any penalties already added.
  2. Pull your Form 11 and compare the square footage, garage and outbuildings with what you actually have. Errors can be fixed through the assessor's office.
  3. Confirm with the auditor that the homestead standard deduction is on the parcel.
  4. Ask your insurer about flood zone status if the house is anywhere near the river, and gather repair records for any water work.
  5. Tell the title company early if taxes are owed, so the payoff is built into the closing statement from the start.

Sellers who would rather skip repairs and showings can price the house for a cash sale. The tax payoff still comes from the proceeds, but the timeline is usually shorter than with a financed buyer.

sections.h2: Tax sale and selling with taxes owed
sections.html:
A county tax sale offers parcels with delinquent taxes to bidders. Floyd County runs its sale entirely online. Bidders register at sriservices.com, and parcel details are on lowtaxinfo.com/floydcounty. Call the treasurer for the next sale date.

An owner who wants a parcel off the list pays the treasurer directly. For parcels eligible for the sale, online and credit card payments are not accepted, so bring cash in exact change or certified funds. The auditor's office keeps tax sale notices, tax sale appeals, records of sale and deeds.

Debt grows before a sale. A late payment draws 5% if made within 30 days with no earlier delinquency, and 10% in other cases. Each later installment date adds another 10% of the unpaid principal, and payments go to tax first, penalties second.

If you sell before the sale date, the title company normally clears the whole balance from your proceeds. Order a payoff from the treasurer early, because the figure changes with each installment date. A cash buyer can close quickly and take the house as is, which helps when the clock is running on a delinquent parcel.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Floyd County?
faqs.a: The Floyd County Treasurer collects it, and the office is in New Albany. Call (812) 948-5477, option 4 for tax payments, to confirm the right address first.

faqs.q: When is the appeal deadline in Floyd County?
faqs.a: June 15, on Form 130 filed with the Floyd County Assessor. Notices of assessment are mailed by April 30.

faqs.q: Can a Floyd County house be sold with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the back tax and penalties from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the treasurer for the current balance so you know what to expect.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty in Floyd County?
faqs.a: It is 5% if you pay within 30 days of the due date and have no earlier delinquency, and 10% in other cases. State law adds another 10% of the unpaid tax at later installment dates.

faqs.q: Does the Ohio River affect selling a house in Floyd County?
faqs.a: It can. The river forms the county's southern edge and flooded most of New Albany in 1937. A buyer or lender may ask about flood zone status and insurance for homes near the water.
